O2.reference: Ref-Elm. Gurvich,1989 pt1 p94 pt2 p9.

decision: Retain production for this source review; prioritize a 2025 natural-isotope thermal plus balanced ATcT 1.228 energy candidate and finite substitution as the next scoped step.

identity.state: X 3Sigma_g- ground manifold, with thermal electronic excitation
identity.not: atomic singlet O, O2 singlet-only gas, or condensed oxygen
identity.janaf_ref_meaning: O2(ref) is the thermochemical elemental reference; in the reviewed 1500-4000 K range its ideal-gas thermals apply, and zero elemental formation enthalpy is not zero dissociation energy.
identity.spin: 16O has nuclear spin zero; the published O2 state sum includes the allowed rotational/electronic statistical weights. No extra factor of three or division by a homonuclear symmetry number is applied.
identity.isotope: Use published natural-composition thermals for the candidate diagnostic; pure16O2 Q moments are a separate reconstruction control. No additional isotope mixing entropy is added.

atct.scope: Rounded balanced central value only; full covariance is not propagated. The separate singlet atom page species446 is excluded.

follow_ups: Construct derivative-consistent 2025 natural-isotope molecular thermals with balanced ATcT 1.228 D0, explicitly separating the existing fit residual and physical energy shift.
Run fixed-network finite substitution and independent numerical controls before any O2 curated adoption; the required 2025 tables and ATcT central anchors are already public.
Retain unbound-state, energy-covariance and atmospheric-validation limitations; ancestor access alone is not a source-review merge gate.
limitations: The 15946 O2 levels are unchanged from 2019; this review uses published 2025 tables and does not independently resum all levels.
Natural-isotope tables already contain the Woolley correction and mass-translation entropy; no extra correction is applied.
Unbound-state uncertainty and complete ATcT covariance are not quantified.
Pointwise 2025/ATcT comparison is not a derivative-consistent candidate or a finite equilibrium response.
